newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOUTHERNERA FINDS NEW S.AFRICAN KIMBERLITES.
newsitem.headline: SOUTHERNERA FINDS NEW S.AFRICAN KIMBERLITES.

text.p: SouthernEra Resources Ltd had made major new mine discoveries in South Africa and had secured concessions to rich Angolan finds, group president Christopher Jennings said on Friday.
Addressing an African mining conference, Jennings said the Canadian company this week discovered three new kimberlites at its Klipspringer project near Potgietersrust in Northern Province.
These were about 18 km from its original kimberlite finds on the 250,000 acre project area and indicated that it could contain the longest dyke system in the world.
"We potentially have a new diamond field," Jennings said.
"With these new discoveries, kimberlites are now known to occur in four areas over 30 km apart, confirming the status of the Klipspringer projects area as an important new kimberlite find.
"I think this is going to be a very significant discovery in South Africa and probably the first significant discovery since the new South Africa came in."
The discoveries were unusual in that they ran right from the plains up to a mountain range, which would make mining easier.
A number of valleys crossed at right angles to the kimberlite fissures and as a result SouthernEra believed that it would have much higher production that in the average shaft.

SouthernEra had already recovered 5,000 carats valued at about $100 each with a grade of about 0.84 carats a tonne. The stones were of a "very good size" and although some had spots, other were flawless, Jennings said.
Shaft sinkers had been engaged to help get primary kimberlite samples. This would stretch over the next few months, after which the company would embark on the final feasibility study.
Jennings said the company hopes to be in production next year.
SouthernEra had also been prospecting in Angola, where it had now gained concessions and had the potential of producing diamonds this year.
Angola was "one of the best countries in the world to be exploring for diamonds...there is an absolute high value and great clarity of these diamonds," Jennings said.
